themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike this week
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints jumped to 7 filings THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 211% spike (z-score: 4.36)—signaling a potential acute exposure event or enforcement action in Riverdale/Fieldston that warrants immediate investigation into source and affected housing stock.
evidence: 7 lead complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (211% increase)
Z-score of 4.36 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Lead exposure is a major public health concern in older NYC housing stock
reporting_angles: Investigate which buildings or block faces generated the spike—are they clustered in one neighborhood or scattered?
Contact HPD to determine if this reflects new testing/enforcement or discovery of contamination in previously unidentified units

themes_detail.label: Door/window complaint surge
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints spiked 125% LAST WEEK to 29 filings versus a baseline of 12.9 per week (z-score: 9.98), suggesting a weather event, break-ins, or structural damage affecting multiple residences that requires urgent field reporting.
evidence: 29 door/window complaints filed last week vs. 12.9 weekly baseline (125% increase)
Z-score of 9.98—among the highest statistical anomalies in the dataset
Timing and clustering suggest a common trigger (storm damage, security issue, or building code violation)
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to determine if complaints cluster geographically and identify common cause (storm, vandalism, building failure)
Interview residents and NYPD/HPD to assess whether break-ins or weather damage is driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Tree damage and dead tree crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints exploded 3100% TWO WEEKS AGO (4 vs. 0.1 weekly average) and damaged tree complaints remain elevated at 259% above baseline (13 last week vs. 3.6 avg, z-score: 4.85), indicating a widespread tree health crisis—likely weather-related—that threatens canopy and infrastructure across the district.
evidence: Dead/dying trees: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72—highest in dataset)
Damaged trees: 13 complaints last week vs. 3.6 baseline (259% increase, z-score: 4.85)
Community board budget requests include 'reconstruct or upgrade park amenity' (recurring theme suggesting longstanding infrastructure need)
reporting_angles: Investigate what triggered the spike 2 weeks ago—severe weather, pest infestation, disease outbreak, or deferred maintenance in Parks Dept.
Interview Parks Dept. and arborists about tree health status in Riverdale; assess whether this reflects broader canopy decline or acute event
Check whether tree removal/replacement backlog exists and how long residents wait for response

themes_detail.label: Paint/plaster deterioration spike
themes_detail.summary: Paint and plaster complaints spiked 131% LAST WEEK to 48 filings versus a baseline of 20.8 per week (z-score: 4.69), suggesting widespread building envelope deterioration affecting multiple buildings—consistent with older housing stock in disrepair.
evidence: 48 paint/plaster complaints filed last week vs. 20.8 weekly baseline (131% increase, z-score: 4.69)
Paint/plaster is #10 complaint type overall in 90-day window (294 total), indicating chronic issue
Spike suggests acute deterioration event or seasonal trigger affecting multiple buildings simultaneously
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether spike is building-specific or neighborhood-wide
Interview HPD on enforcement activity: has there been a recent violation notice blitz or inspection push?
Assess whether water damage from recent weather events (which may explain tree damage spike) is driving interior deterioration complaints

themes_detail.label: Root damage and sidewalk collapse risk
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints surged 1500% TWO WEEKS AGO (4 complaints vs. 0.2 baseline, z-score: 5.67), indicating a concentrated risk of pedestrian injury or infrastructure failure—likely linked to the tree damage spike and warranting sidewalk audit.
evidence: Root/sewer/sidewalk complaints: 4 filings 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Timing overlaps with dead/dying tree spike (both 2 weeks ago), suggesting root-related damage as common cause
Street Condition remains high-volume complaint (943 total over 90 days), indicating ongoing infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: Request DOT sidewalk condition audit data for the district; determine which blocks have trip/collapse hazards
Interview residents on affected blocks about damage and city response timeline
Investigate whether root damage remediation requires tree removal and whether removal creates new infrastructure gaps
